top_news.title: Psychological methods reveal major weaknesses in AI security testing
top_news.dek: Researchers found that current AI safety benchmarks are easily gamed by models that simply block more requests to artificially inflate safety scores.
top_news.brief: A study from the UK AI Security Institute applied psychometric testing methods to eight popular LLM safety benchmarks. The analysis reveals that these tests often fail to measure consistent traits, as models can achieve higher safety scores by broadly refusing prompts rather than demonstrating genuine alignment. The researchers propose a new methodology to detect models that exhibit performative caution during testi…
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing the relationship between model refusal rates and safety benchmark scores.

top_news.title: llm-openrouter 0.7
top_news.dek: The llm-openrouter CLI tool has been updated to version 0.7, adding support for displaying reasoning traces.
top_news.brief: The latest release of the llm-openrouter plugin is now compatible with LLM 0.32. This update allows users to view reasoning traces for models accessed through the OpenRouter API directly within the CLI.
top_news.image_alt: Terminal interface showing LLM reasoning output

top_news.title: Agents, Workers - Choose OAuth scopes for Wrangler and the Cloudflare API MCP server
top_news.dek: Cloudflare now supports optional OAuth scopes for Wrangler and the Cloudflare API MCP server, allowing for more granular permission control.
top_news.brief: Users can now selectively grant or revoke optional OAuth scopes during the authorization process for Wrangler and the Cloudflare API MCP server. The updated consent dialog includes an 'Edit Permissions' feature, enabling developers to restrict access to specific resources while keeping required scopes enabled.
top_news.image_alt: Cloudflare OAuth consent dialog showing the Edit Permissions interface.

top_news.title: An AI tool for prioritizing candidate biomarkers from wearable sensor data
top_news.dek: Google Research introduces the Biomarker Discovery Framework to automate the identification of clinically meaningful biomarkers from wearable sensor data.
top_news.brief: The framework addresses the limitations of existing LLM-based agents, which often struggle with physiological time-series data by prioritizing predictive performance over statistical validity. It aims to reduce spurious correlations and brittle features, enabling more reliable analysis of continuous physiological signals like heart rate and sleep patterns.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing the Biomarker Discovery Framework workflow for processing wearable sensor data.

top_news.title: New MCP Roadmap
top_news.dek: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) team has released an updated roadmap detailing development priorities for the coming months.
top_news.brief: The updated roadmap focuses on five key areas, including server-initiated events, result type improvements, and agent identity. These features aim to enhance protocol functionality and address items previously listed as on the horizon by the core maintainers and working groups.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing the Model Context Protocol development roadmap priority areas.
